Lower half: angles from 180° to 360° (or negatively from -180° to 0).

Green ray 1: lower left, around 200-210° (i.e., -150° to -160°). Green ray 2: lower right, around -40° (i.e., 320°). Black ray: downward, slightly left: around -105°? Hmm, in the figure the black ray from O goes to about (288, 625)? O is at (360, 360). The endpoint of the black ray is about (288, 625). Direction: dx = -72, dy = +265 (downward). Angle: atan2(-265, -72) in standard math coordinates (y up): point is (288, 625) in image coordinates, y down. Converting: math coordinates y up: dy = -(625-360) = -265. So direction (-72, -265): angle = atan2(-265, -72) ≈ 180° + 74.8°? Calculation: atan(265/72) = atan(3.68) ≈ 74.8°, third quadrant: angle ≈ 180° + 74.8° = 254.8°, i.e., -105.2°.

Green ray 1 endpoint ~ (120, 497): dx = -240, dy = -(497-360) = -137. Angle = atan2(-137, -240) ≈ 180° + 29.7° = 209.7°, i.e., -150.3°. Hmm, but the 30° label: angle between OB (180°) and green ray 1 (209.7°) is about 30°. Yes! So the 30° angle is between ray OB and green ray 1.

Green ray 2 endpoint ~ (573, 537): dx = 213, dy = -177. Angle = atan2(-177, 213) ≈ -39.7°, i.e., about -40°. The 40° label is between OA (0°) and green ray 2: yes, 40°.

65°: between the black ray (-105°) and green ray 2 (-40°): difference = 65°. Yes.

Shaded sector: between green ray 1 (-150°) and the black ray (-105°): difference = 45°? Wait, -150.3 to -105.2 is 45.1°. Hmm, but let me check the total: lower half is 180°. Probability = 45/360 = 1/8.

Wait, but the shaded sector is between green ray 1 and the black ray: yes, the gray region is between the lower-left green ray and the black ray. So central angle = 45°. Probability = 45/360 = 1/8.

Hmm, but let me check the arcs in the figure: the arc for 30° is between OB and green ray 1? The arc drawn near O on the left: from about (305,360) to (310, 385)? Arc for 40°: on the right side, from OA (0°) to green ray 2 (-40°): the arc is from (437,360) to (420, 405)? Yes.

Arc for 65°: between the black ray and green ray 2: arc from (355, 415) to (405, 400)? Yes.

content:
Looking at the lower half of the circle (below diameter AB), the straight angle at O is 180°.

The angles below the diameter, going from OB to OA, are:
- 30° (between OB and the first green radius),
- the shaded sector's angle (between the first green radius and the black radius),
- 65° (between the black radius and the second green radius),
- 40° (between the second green radius and OA).

So the shaded central angle = 180° − 30° − 65° − 40° = 45°.

The probability equals the ratio of the sector's angle to the full circle:
P = 45° / 360° = 1/8.

\boxed{1/8}
